newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell, BP Rotterdam refining back to full capacity.
newsitem.headline: Shell, BP Rotterdam refining back to full capacity.

text.p: Shell and BP have returned to full capacity crude throughput at their Rotterdam refineries as a result of slightly healthier margins and expectations of further near term improvements, trade sources said on Tuesday.
"It's back to normal. Healthier margins are the reason," one source said.
Texaco meanwhile is still running its Rotterdam operations at 20 percent below capacity, as it has done since the middle of May, although it is continuing to monitor the improving situation.
"We are reassessing it every day and haven't decided to come back up yet, although (margins) are looking better," said a trader familiar with the refinery's operations.
Last week, Shell cut crude throughput at its 370,000 barrel per day (bpd) Pernis refinery in Rotterdam by "roughly 14 percent" due to poor operating margins.
In the middle of the previous week, BP cut crude throughput in Rotterdam by about 40 percent, equivalent to a 10 percent cut for the month of May.
BP owns 65 percent of BP/Texaco joint venture Nerefco whose refineries have a total capacity of 420,000 bpd.
On May 23, Rotterdam refinery margins for a complex cracking refinery hit a two and a half month low of $1.03 a barrel. The margin at simple refineries at the time was below zero.
Last week, the average complex margin was $1.68, heading above $2 at the end of the week -- but this was still lower than the April average of $2.32.
Some traders say this margin still renders full throughput refining uneconomic. Only the prospect of near-term improvement justifies the latest moves.
"Margins have barely improved. We are however anticipating healthier margins," said a trader with a Rotterdam-based major.
